rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act rent cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, and no more than twice in that period. New tenancies may start at any rent. Buildings with a certificate of occupancy in the last 15 years, housing under stricter local rent control and certain other housing are exempt.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower
rules.effective_date_note: Original cap applied to increases on or after 2019-03-15 (operative 2020-01-01 per TPA); the current version (SB 567) was effective 2024-01-01 and operative 2024-04-01 per the statute text. Repealed 2030-01-01 by its terms.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; CO within previous 15 years; separately alienable property not owned by REIT/corporation/corporate-member LLC with notice; owner-occupied duplex; mobilehome owner-occupants.
rules.penalty: Injunctive relief, damages equal to overcharge (up to 3x if willful), attorney's fees; AG/city attorney/county counsel may enforce.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where local rent control restricts annual increases to less than the state cap; does not expand or limit local authority under Civ. Code ch. 2.7 (Costa-Hawkins).

unverifiable_exemptions: single-family homes and condos not owned by REIT, corporation or corporate-member LLC

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act – just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: After a tenant has lived in a unit for 12 months, the owner may end the tenancy only for a stated at-fault or no-fault just cause. For no-fault reasons the owner must pay one month's rent in relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent, and the notice must say so.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; no-fault relocation = 1 month's rent
rules.quoted_span: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy
rules.effective_date_note: Original TPA effective 2020-01-01 (not stated in the section text); current version operative 2024-04-01 and amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities; dormitories; owner shares bathroom/kitchen; owner-occupied single-family and duplex; CO within previous 15 years; separately alienable property of non-corporate owner with notice; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.penalty: Noncompliant notice is void; actual damages, attorney's fees, up to 3x damages if willful; AG/city attorney/county counsel may seek injunctions.
rules.interaction: Does not apply where a local just-cause ordinance adopted on or before 9/1/2019, or a later more protective one, applies; property cannot be subject to both.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable single-family homes/condos of non-corporate owner with notice
dormitories, hospitals, care facilities, transient hotels

rules.title: California security deposit cap (AB 12) and return rules
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security above one month's rent (two months for qualifying small landlords with no more than two properties and four units total, except for service members). Deposits must be returned with an itemized statement within 21 days after the tenant vacates.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy
rules.effective_date_note: Cap applies to security collected on or after 2024-07-01 (AB 12); current text amended by AB 414 effective 2026-01-01.
rules.penalty: Bad-faith retention may bring statutory damages up to twice the deposit plus actual damages.

coverage.landlord_size_condition: Two-month cap only for a natural person or LLC of natural persons owning no more than 2 rental properties with no more than 4 units total
unverifiable_exemptions: small landlord status for two-month cap

rules.title: California application screening fee limits
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only up to actual out-of-pocket costs and never more than $30 per applicant, adjusted annually for CPI. No fee if no unit is available; landlord must give an itemized receipt, refund unused amounts, and provide a copy of the credit report.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted since 1998 (Berkeley Rent Board lists $68.96 for 2026)
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant
rules.effective_date_note: Date of the AB 1170 amendment; the cap itself dates from earlier versions.
rules.conflict_note: The statute states only the $30 base; the CPI-adjusted figure is not stated in the statute. A Berkeley Rent Board page (D005) gives $68.96 as the 2026 maximum; no single official statewide figure confirmed.

rules.title: FEHA source-of-income protections (incl. subsidy credit-history rule)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against or harass applicants or tenants based on source of income, including Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers. For subsidized tenants, income standards must be based on the tenant's share of rent, and applicants must be allowed to offer alternative evidence instead of credit history.
rules.key_value: ban on source-of-income discrimination incl. Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person
rules.effective_date_note: Source-of-income definition expanded to government subsidies by SB 329 effective 2020-01-01 (per D015); SB 267 amendment (HUD-VASH, credit-history option) effective 2024-01-01 per D027.
rules.exemptions: Owner occupying a home and renting to one additional person; shared living areas; senior housing.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied home renting to one additional person

rules.title: California Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations (housing)
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history only within strict limits: blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.key_value: no blanket bans on criminal records; no consideration of arrests without convictions
rules.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2 (Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations)
citation_aliases: Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions
rules.effective_date_note: Document says the regulations took effect Jan. 1, 2020.
rules.review_note: The document does not state the regulation section number, so the regulation is cited by name only.

rules.title: AB 325 / SB 763 – Common pricing algorithm prohibition (Cartwright Act)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (software used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to influence prices) as part of a conspiracy to restrain trade, or to use or distribute one while coercing others to adopt its recommended prices. Applies to apartment rental pricing software among other industries.
rules.key_value: ban on common pricing algorithms using competitor data to collude or coerce
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter
rules.effective_date_note: Chaptered 2025-10-06; D028 states the laws took effect January 1, 2026.
rules.penalty: Criminal fines up to $6 million (corporations) or $1 million (individuals), or twice gain/loss if greater; civil fines up to $1 million in AG/DA actions; treble damages in private suits (per D028).
rules.exemptions: End consumers; single-firm algorithms using only the business's own data.

parsed.notes: Consolidated CA: 4 duplicate security/fee/algorithm/source-of-income candidates merged by statute section. Criminal-history regulations kept separate from Gov. Code § 12955. No no-rule findings: every category has an enacted state rule in the provided documents.
